status: preregistration; no readout fitted on any feature this study introduces
what_this_task_is: a perception/representation readability test of one frozen, externally pretrained encoder against its same-architecture random-init floor; trains nothing; collects no corpus; preregisters no control formulation
claim_scope: readability of the post-look apple by kernel ridge on 190 roots, beyond the architecture's random init; not prediction by a world model, not control, not closed-loop behaviour

predecessor.recommended_next: one preregistered test of an externally pretrained frozen encoder against its own random-init floor, on this probe, before any corpus

A_tok.reading: meets the bars, not the floor

predecessor.reported_only_context: token features of a ViT, even random-init ones, expose the post-look apple on this probe (F-tok); the information is lost at the pooled 128-d latent. Given no row.

question: does a frozen encoder pretrained elsewhere (never on this corpus) expose the apple in TASK-061's post-look 112 px frame to TASK-061's readouts under the unchanged TASK-059 bars, and beat a random-init encoder of the same architecture read at the same point
